title: OpenBikeComputer map catalog (schema_version 2)
description: The schema_version 2 map catalog: one schema, a set of skins, named cell-set regions with drawable boundaries, and digest-pinned per-band cell indices. A consumer prices a selection from this document alone — total bytes and bytes per band, which is the per-file projection a volume set needs — and verifies each satellite against the `bytes` + `sha256` pinned here. The satellite documents are `$defs/CellIndexDocument`, `$defs/RegionCellsDocument` and `$defs/TerrainIndexDocument`. The optional `terrain` block is a second artifact class on its own revision track (§13). Normative contract: OBCC_Spec.md, with OBCA_Spec.md for the grid, bands, and assembly and OBCT_Spec.md for the raster.

schema_version.description: Envelope version, `2`. Checked before any other field.

generated_at.description: When this root was generated, RFC 3339 UTC — the only wall clock on the generation path (`OBCC_Spec.md` §3).

schema.description: The catalog's **single** schema. Not an array: the hosted store carries the 7-LOD bikepacking ladder and nothing else, because a second schema would make the whole planet-shaped cell store exist twice (§3, epic #1016 D2).

skins.description: Every skin offered, sorted by `id`. Inlined rather than referenced: one is ≈ 2 KB and a builder needs all of them at once to draw a picker.

cell_index.description: One entry per band, sorted by `cell_log2` descending (§8).

terrain.description: The terrain artifact class, when the catalog publishes one (§13). Absent is a complete, valid catalog: every consumer degrades to "no elevation here", which is exactly what a map with no terrain has always done.

network_terrain_revision.description: **The one coupling between the two revision tracks** (§13.4). Network-band cells are baked sampling OBCT, so their `Ascent M` values are a function of a particular terrain revision; this records which one. `None` for a terrain-less bake, whose ascents are all zero and depend on nothing. It is at the root rather than in [`SchemaEntry`] on purpose: the schema is the identity of the OBCM store and must not acquire a terrain field, or a terrain re-bake would look like a schema change to every consumer that compares schemas.

SchemaEntry.description: The schema: the identity of the cell store. Everything a consumer needs to price a selection and an assembler needs to stamp a skin, with no out-of-band constant (§4).

revision.description: Monotone content revision. Every cell states the revision it was baked at, and a bump invalidates the whole store — assembly copies chunk bytes between files, which is only meaningful within one revision (`OBCA_Spec.md` §6.3).

obcm_version.description: OBCM format version, read from the **cells' own headers**; every cell agrees or generation fails (§10).

grid.description: The grid's constants, restated so no consumer hard-codes them.

bands.description: The band table: which LODs and which non-geometry sections live in which cell size, and which file of a volume set they assemble into.

styles.description: The canonical style-id assignment. `obc-pack` numbers feature types 1-based in config document order and every feature header in every chunk references those ids, so the assignment is part of the cells' bytes — schema data, never skin data (§4).

routing.description: Routing facts baked into the cells. The island-prune threshold is schema data: two cells pruned at different thresholds do not assemble into a graph with consistent semantics (`OBCA_Spec.md` §3.5).

chunk_size.description: The per-LOD chunk capacity bound the cells were written with (`OBCM_Spec.md` §3). An assembler re-checks every copied offset pair against it.

GridEntry.description: `OBCA_Spec.md` §1.1's constants. Published so a consumer computing a cell's square or an assembly bbox never hard-codes a power of two.

LodEntry.description: One rung of the LOD ladder.

max_mpp.description: Meters-per-pixel upper bound; `null` for the `+inf` coarsest level (`OBCM_Spec.md` §3).

band.description: The band whose cells carry this LOD.

BandEntry.description: One band: a cell size plus the content its cells carry.

id.description: Stable band id, e.g. `fine`. Also the band's segment in a cell URL.

lods.description: Ladder LODs this band's cells carry, ascending. Empty for the `core` band.

sections.description: Non-geometry sections this band's cells carry. Only the `core` band has any.

role.description: Which file of a volume set this band becomes.

BandSection.description: A non-geometry OBCM section a band may carry.

BandRole.description: Which file of a volume set a band's content assembles into (`OBCA_Spec.md` §5.1).

oneOf.description: The one unsplittable file: nav graph, POIs, style table. Carries no LOD, because its headroom under `4 GiB − 1` is the design's hard limit.
The single whole-assembly coarse shard that keeps a zoomed-out viewport a one-file read.
An ordinary geometry shard's content; splits by bbox as needed.

StyleAssignment.description: One feature type's canonical style id — the assignment baked into every chunk.

id.description: 1-based style id, as referenced by feature headers (`OBCM_Spec.md` §2, §5.2).

RoutingEntry.description: The routing facts a cell's nav bytes were produced under.

min_component_edges.description: Island-prune threshold, applied at **assembly** over the merged graph (`OBCA_Spec.md` §3.5/§4.6) — a cell bake prunes only strictly interior components.

SkinEntry.description: A skin is stamped onto ~2 KB of an assembly at assembly time, so it is baked into nothing and invalidates nothing.

version.description: The skin's content version. No cell carries a skin.

styles.description: One entry per `schema.styles` feature type, in schema id order. A skin that misses one would ship a map with an invisible layer; one that names a feature type the schema lacks is stale (§5).

preview.description: Optional digest-pinned rendered sample. It is presentation only and never participates in cell selection or assembly.

SkinStyle.description: One feature type's presentation values — the bytes of a style record a skin owns (colors, weight, z, priority and the `Flags` bits). The **id** is not here: it belongs to the schema, and a skin may not renumber it (`OBCA_Spec.md` §4.7).

fixed_width.description: Style-record flag bit 4 (#1095): the weight is used verbatim on screen, off the zoom width ramp. Defaulted so a catalog written before the bit existed still parses.

terrain_layer.description: Style-record flag bit 5 (#1095): part of the suppressible terrain layer.

contour_index.description: Style-record flag bit 6 (v13, #1105): the index contours. Like the id, this is the schema's fact and not the skin's — it is republished here only so an assembler restamping a style table has every bit of the record in one place. Defaulted, as the two above are.

color2.description: Optional RGB565 secondary color; `null` when the style has none.

SkinPreview.description: One skin rendered over the bakery's canonical map scene.

RegionEntry.description: A named region: a boundary to draw and a cell set to fetch (§6).

id.description: Slash-separated id, matching the extract hierarchy.

parent.description: The enclosing region's id, when the curation nests.

boundary.description: Simplified outline for drawing (§7). Presentation only.

bytes.description: Total bytes of every cell in this region's set, across all bands.

bytes_by_band.description: Those bytes per band, summing to `bytes`. This is what makes the §5.7 pre-download projection *per file* rather than merely per set: a volume set's roles partition by band, so the `core` band's bytes are the core file's bytes.

partial_cell_count_by_band.description: Partial cells per band, including zeroes for fully covered bands.

terrain.description: This region's terrain footprint (§13.3), when the catalog publishes terrain.

cells_url.description: Where the region's cell-id list lives (§6).

cells_bytes.description: Size of that document, in bytes.

cells_sha256.description: Its digest — the pin that keeps the satellite all-or-nothing.

Boundary.description: A region's simplified outline, in integer microdegrees, `[lat, lon]` per point. Presentation only: it MUST NOT be used to compute a cell set (that is stored, §6), to price a selection, or as a packer input bbox. The coverage outline a builder draws for a live selection is a different object — the union of the selected cells' squares, computed client-side — and is deliberately not in the catalog.

tolerance_udeg.description: The tolerance the outline was reduced at.

rings.description: One or more closed rings; the first is an exterior and any ring nested in it is a hole. A region that is several disjoint pieces repeats that pattern.

RegionTerrain.description: A region's terrain footprint, when the catalog publishes terrain. Kept out of `bytes`/`bytes_by_band`, which are the OBCM volume set's per-file projection: a rider may take the map without the raster, so the two prices are separate numbers.

bytes.description: Sum of the real bytes of this region's downloadable terrain cells.

CellIndexRef.description: The root's pin on one band's cell index (§8).

cell_count.description: Downloadable OBCM artifact entries in the referenced document.

known_empty_count.description: Canonical cells represented as verified-empty ranges rather than OBCM artifacts.

sha256.description: Its digest. A satellite that does not match MUST be rejected and the root kept.

TerrainEntry.description: The terrain artifact class (OBCC_Spec.md §13): an OBCT raster on the same OBCA grid, published with its OWN revision track. `dataset_version`, `posting_log2`, `cell_log2` and `terrain_revision` are terrain's entire lockstep rule — no OBCM version or schema revision appears here, and an OBCM or schema bump invalidates none of these objects. The single reverse coupling is the root's `network_terrain_revision`, which records the terrain revision the nav graph's ascents were integrated from.

dataset_id.description: Stable kebab-case id of the source dataset, e.g. `copernicus-glo-30`.

dataset_version.description: That dataset's release identity, e.g. `2021-1`. Opaque to a consumer: it is compared for equality, never parsed.

cell_log2.description: `log2(S)` of the terrain cell, µdeg. Independent of any band's `cell_log2`.

terrain_revision.description: Monotone content revision of the terrain store, bumped by a re-bake. Unrelated to `schema.revision`: neither invalidates the other (§13.2).

attribution.description: The source licence's required credit, verbatim, so a consumer displays it from the catalog rather than hard-coding a string that can go stale (§13.5).

cell_index.description: The single pinned terrain cell index.

TerrainIndexRef.description: The root's pin on the terrain cell index — the §8 machinery, one document instead of one per band, because terrain has no bands.

cell_count.description: Downloadable OBCT artifact entries in the referenced document.

known_empty_count.description: Canonical cells represented as all-`NODATA` runs rather than OBCT artifacts.

CellEntry.description: One published cell. There is deliberately no bbox: a cell's coverage is exactly its grid square, which the `id` determines to the microdegree (OBCA_Spec.md §1.3), and the generator verifies the artifact's own OBCM header bbox against it at bake time. A stored copy could only agree (redundant) or disagree (a lie).

built_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC, recorded by the bake job.

sources.description: Every source extract this cell was baked from, sorted by `extract_id`.

partial.description: `true` iff those sources do not fully cover the cell's square (`OBCA_Spec.md` §3.7). A consumer MUST NOT present a partial cell as canonical coverage.

CellSource.description: One source extract behind a cell.

KnownEmptyRun.description: An inclusive row run of cells proven to carry no content for one band. Empty coverage is explicit because absence means a coverage hole. Runs avoid publishing both an OBCM object and one JSON entry for every empty ocean or network cell in a planet catalog.

start.description: First canonical cell id in the run.

end.description: Last canonical cell id in the run (inclusive, same row as `start`).

built_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC, recorded by the bake job.

sources.description: Every source extract against which emptiness was established.

schema_revision.description: The revision every cell in this document was baked at.

known_empty.description: Canonical, non-overlapping row runs that carry no bytes for this band.

CellIndexDocument.description: A band's cell index: the satellite the root pins (§8).

terrain.description: Sorted terrain cell ids on the terrain grid (§13.3). A separate field rather than a `cells` key: `cells` is keyed by *schema band*, and terrain is not a band — it has no LOD, no section, no assembly role and no schema revision.

RegionCellsDocument.description: A region's cell list: the satellite `RegionEntry::cells_url` points at (§6). Cell ids only — every other fact is in the band's index, keyed by the same id.

TerrainCellEntry.description: One published terrain cell. No bbox and no source list: the `id` is the square (§13.1), and the provenance is one dataset stated once in the root block rather than repeated on every one of thousands of entries.

id.description: Canonical cell id, `<cell_log2>/<i>/<j>`, on the terrain grid.

built_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC, recorded by the bake job.

TerrainEmptyRun.description: An inclusive row run of terrain cells that are all `NODATA` — open ocean, which [`obc-dem`](https://github.com/timohueser/OpenBikeComputer) does not write an object for at all (`OBCT_Spec.md` §4.3 makes an absent cell and an all-void one answer identically). The catalog says so instead, so a hole is still distinguishable from a coverage gap.

known_empty.description: Canonical, non-overlapping row runs whose every sample is `NODATA` — ocean.

TerrainIndexDocument.description: The terrain cell index: the satellite the root's terrain block pins (§13.1). It restates the four lockstep fields so the document is self-describing when it is fetched on its own, and it deliberately carries **no** `schema_revision`: a terrain cell does not know which OBCM schema it is being used beside, and adding the field would make an OBCM bump rewrite this document.
